content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency > 4.0s for route /v1/generate (prod-us-west). Current window: 10m. SLO burn: 18%. Trigger: latency-p99-threshold. PagerDuty: PD-2345

pagerduty: PagerDuty: PD-2345 triggered by monitor latency-p99-threshold. Page sent to #eng-oncall rotation. Incident links: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-2345

sam: acked PD-2345 (taking). I see p95 creeping up too. Digging into recent rolling deploys and autoscaler metrics.

asha: on it — checking pod restarts and tokenization queue. Early signal: KV cache eviction spikes ~7999001200. Could be hotkey churn.

mike: i'm also looking at autoscaler logs, CPU/GPU util jumped in west, and we have several small pods OOMing around 7999001185. No config rollbacks yet.

liz: customer impact from support: a few customers reported timeouts on long-form generation, some http 504s. Not widespread but visible for high-token requests.

sam: quick mitigation idea: enable temporary regional fallthrough to eu-west for new requests and reduce max_tokens default to 1024 for the route. That should lower tail latency while we stabilize. Anyone object?

asha: +1 for fallthrough. Also propose disabling prefix KV caching for the hottest model instance to stop thrash — can toggle via runtime flag x-kv-cache-enabled=false.

mike: i can patch the routing rule now. Command i'll run: 

```
# enable fallthrough to eu-west for prod-us-west
curl -X POST "https://platform.internal/api/v1/routing/enable-fallthrough" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLAT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"from":"prod-us-west","to":"prod-eu-west","routes":["/v1/generate"]}'
```

mike: and to reduce default tokens config: 

```
# update route config
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/gateway ROUTE_MAX_TOKENS=1024 --record
```

sam: mike, go ahead. ash a, can you toggle the kv-cache flag after fallthrough is live? i'll monitor SLO dashboards.

asha: will do. toggling now. patch: 

```
# disable kv cache for model svc-prod-gen-3
curl -X PATCH "https://runtime.internal/models/svc-prod-gen-3/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNTIME_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"kv_cache_enabled":false}'
```

asha: done. I also added a short spike-protection rule to the sidecar to reject 2-in-5s bursts per token key.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: ACTION: fallthrough enabled to prod-eu-west for /v1/generate. KV cache disabled for svc-prod-gen-3. Autoscaler recommendations: add 6 extra slots to burst pool.

sam: monitoring... p99 dropped from 4.2s -> 2.1s in the last 90s. p95 now ~320ms. SLO burn dropping. Good signal.

liz: coordinated with support to message customers queued requests may retry; CS draft sent to customers affected. Oliver, pls confirm no escalations.

oliver: confirmed, only a handful of premium accounts hit timeouts. CS is sending templated note and offering priority retries. No active escalations yet.

mike: i'm provisioning temporary burst capacity (GPU pool) and patching autoscaler: 

```
# bump reserved burst
curl -X POST "https://infra.internal/autoscaler/burst" -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN" -d '{"pool":"prod-west-burst","add":6}'
```

mike: patch applied, new instances booting (IDs: i-0a1b2c3d, i-0e4f5a6b).

asha: i see fewer evictions and the tokenizer queue drain rate improved. tail latency stabilizing. Will keep an eye for 15m.

sam: PD-2345 update: primary mitigation applied. Next: decide whether to rollback the last config deploy that went out ~7999001100 (model flags + cache tweak). I'm leaning to let runtime patching stay and revisit deploy in morning unless we see regression. Thoughts?

liz: agree to avoid rollback since mitigation helped. If we can get postmortem showing root cause is hotkey-induced KV thrash we can put in circuit-breaker guards before next deploy.

asha: logging shows the deploy changed prefix hashing which increased hotkey collisions. Root cause likely that hashing change + cache sizing mistake. I'll capture traces and add to postmortem.

sam: ok i'll start handoff notes. Oncall next shift is @mike in 25 minutes. i'll leave all runbook steps in this thread and mark checkpoints.

sam: CHECKPOINTS: 1) confirm p99 < 2.5s for 10m window 2) ensure no new 504 spikes 3) verify burst pool stabilized 4) collect traces + logs for postmortem link

mike: taking next shift. i'll watch metrics and prepare rollback plan but won't execute unless we see re-escalation. Please DM me any urgent changes.

incident-bot: :information_source: PD-2345 status: acknowledged by sam. Current severity: high. Next notification window: 5m.

sam: leaving a final note: estimated customer impact: intermittent timeouts for long-token generations for ~0.8% of traffic windows between 7999001100-7999001230. Root cause suspected: prefix-hash change in deploy that increased hotkey collisions -> KV eviction thrash. Postmortem to follow (link will be added).

mike: handing off: i'll run the 15m stabilization checklist and then add mitigation as an automated playbook if this pattern repeats.

asha: adding logs/traces to the incident channel and will draft the postmortem with timeline.

sam: thanks all — keep this thread updated with any regressions. If things re-escalate, PD-2345 will auto-escalate per policy.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PD-2345 mitigation applied. Monitoring continues.
